concepts.name: crt-service-idle
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup, image edit of the actual game screenshot.
Primary request: revise Club Mutant's UI so it harmonizes with the ACTUAL low-resolution hazy CRT game, rather than overpowering it.
Reference 1 is the target screenshot. Preserve its actual game image, character, red brick walls, yellow grid floor, existing tan/olive convex CRT bezel, camera, warm soft grain, curved screen opening, and composition as closely as possible. Do not improve, sharpen, enlarge or redesign the 3D world. Keep the FULL existing CRT frame visible including all four corners. Do not put another outer frame around the screenshot.
Reference 2 is an ACTUAL 128px Blender-rendered KonpyuuTA OS settings icon; preserve this small, slightly soft, chunky prerendered 3D character. Reference 3 is the existing brand logo: its flower and irregular skeletal lettering are accents, NOT a reason to add a giant banner.
Art direction: subtle industrial/electronic Winamp skin plus old CRT service terminal, a handmade mid-1990s personal-site touch. A quiet blend of wire, a few aged metal chain-link clasps, and occasional flower/insect ornaments. MOSTLY plain readable surfaces. No large literal medieval thorns in this revision.
Resolution/material target: objects should look like 32-to-64-pixel prerendered sprites, modest color ramps, slight dither and softness, lit by the SAME warm muted ambient light as the room. Soft dull gray-green metal and brownish charcoal plastic harmonize with the existing monitor. Small muted red and dusty blue insulated wires, a little worn solder and screws, small dark beetle. NOT shiny high-resolution jewel chrome, not razor-sharp bevels, not bright acid green, not dramatic fantasy lighting.
Crucial visual hierarchy: the 3D room and character are the focal point. Quiet compact controls only. Recreate current screenshot footprint, keep most (at least 80%) of the original image unobscured. No oversized panels, no giant logo, no ornate frame repeated around every individual widget. Ornament occupies at most a few pixels along an edge. Keep small TEXT legible, calm, warm off-white terminal monospace, muted olive-green LCD digits. Material assets may be slightly low-res, text must not be unreadable.
Precise scale relative to 1455x730 source: player about 300x70px, dock icons 24-30px, text 12-13px equivalent, thin wire 2-3px, beetle 10-14px. There should be NO large 100px 3D icons. Do not add arrows or explanatory captions. No external computer/laptop mockup. Do not add new world objects.
Keep action icons recognizable as tiny physical 3D controls with simple symbols. Keep green and violet as sparse status lights. No emoji. Leave actual perspective and original low-resolution world intact.
Output a front-on wide screenshot at the same approximate 2:1 aspect ratio as target, not a zoomed crop.
State: QUIET EVERYDAY PLAY. Only a compact player in the original top-left region, a tiny button dock in the original right-edge region, and a small bottom-center chat input. No open playlist, no open chat log, no DJ queue.
Player: roughly 300x70px at x18 y18 relative to the source, a plain dark brown-gray plastic faceplate, one small recessed olive phosphor track/time display reading "Malibu — One Life" and "03:43", a thin seek line, small metal play/stop/skip controls and a subdued physical volume knob. A tiny 22px green prerendered Club Mutant flower (intended for slow rotation) sits at its left edge. Thin dull red and dusty blue wires lie along only the upper-left and lower-right edges, terminating in little plugs. One small beetle at a connector. No header banner. It should feel much closer in size and weight to the existing mini-player than to a full Winamp window.
Right dock: retain original narrow vertical footprint on beige monitor side bezel; replace generic flat outline icons with small low-res prerendered disc/chat bubble/mechanical cog/speaker/exit objects. Physical shallow sockets, muted green/violet tiny indicators, not floating modern rounded squares.
Bottom composer: retain original current small 390px wide, 34px high footprint on the lower bezel; simple charcoal terminal inset, text "Press Enter to chat", a tiny wire clip and a small flower indicator.
Entire UI very restrained, soft, integrated, no extra ornate border or chain around the screen. Most of the unchanged screenshot must remain visible.

State: CONTEXTUAL PLAYLIST WINDOW OPEN, still showing nearly all the game and whole original CRT border. The only larger window is a floating compact playlist at the lower-left of the game opening, about 285px wide by 235px tall relative to the 1455x730 source, positioned x125 y350. Player stays small (300x70px) at x18 y18 as in the quiet state: olive phosphor display reading "Malibu — One Life" and "03:43", small metal play/stop/skip buttons, modest flower sprite, thin red/blue wire pair at two corners.
Playlist window: simple brownish charcoal old terminal service-box faceplate, thin inset bevel, one tiny linked metal clasp, a muted red cable and dusty blue wire threaded down just one edge. An almost insect-like joint and a small dull flower shape at a corner suggest the earlier gothic taste in a subtle industrial way. One low-res tiny beetle on an external wire. No ornate medieval fantasy border, no large thorns, no decorative logo. Title "PLAYLISTS"; small close and minimize buttons. Tabs "tracks", "search", "link". Compact legible track rows "Enya — Only Time", "Return of the Silkie", "DJ LOSTBOI — PET SHOP B", "dreamloader — sky2k", with small durations and restrained olive selection tint. Bottom status "+ add to queue". Text and control sizes consistent with existing game UI, not giant.
Right dock: 24-30px low-res physical disc/chat bubble/cog/speaker/exit icons on existing beige bezel, no full-height panel. Bottom small existing-position chat input "Press Enter to chat". No other panel open. No added full-screen frame.
Make the skin feel like a lovingly modified secondhand CRT terminal rather than a heroic fantasy music player. Full original rounded screen edge and all corners remain visible.
